evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-07-29) management said the H2 cloud-communications guide ($622-626m FY) assumes growth 'slightly less than the first half growth rate' and called it conservative, because it excludes the Salesforce Agentforce Contact Center ramp and the five newest $1m+ enterprise wins. They also said two 2025 customers would exit 2026 at nearly twice their originally estimated contract value. Salesforce has since announced (2026-09-16) a rollout to 25+ countries 'this fall'. That sets up a fourth consecutive raise of the FY revenue/EBITDA guide. The bar is the guide midpoint ($233m Q3 revenue, $905m FY).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-04-30): beat and raise, +52.1%. Q2 2026 (2026-07-29): revenue beat (+1.2% vs consensus), FY revenue and EBITDA raised, FY EPS trimmed for share count, political cut from $15m to $13m: -29.3%. So a raise alone has not protected the stock; the read is on the quality of cloud-communications growth and the EPS line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($233.1m), so the street has not modelled the excluded Salesforce and new-deal ramps. A market pricing a raise would not have the stock 17.6% lower over 20 days with Hold initiations ('price already reflects much of the growth', Morgan Stanley 2026-10-16). Pricing it would look like a consensus above the guide range.
evidence.independence: Salesforce/Bandwidth international rollout release, 2026-09-16, a different document: https://techintelpro.com/news/Cloud/Cloud-AI/bandwidth-salesforce-expand-global-rollout-of-native-contact-center. evidence.text: Q2 Voice Solutions revenue was $121m, up only 9% year on year, a slowdown from Q1 that management blamed on enterprise ramp timing. The AI-voice narrative that carried the stock from about $13 to $78 needs voice growth to reaccelerate in Q3. A second quarter near 9% is the most likely trigger for a repeat of the -29% Q2 reaction, even with total revenue at the guide. What would have to go right elsewhere: messaging (commercial +18% in Q2) and software services (+66%) are already carrying the growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print, where voice decelerated to 9%, moved -29.3% despite a total-revenue beat and raise. Q1 2026, with strong AI-voice commentary, moved +52.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 20-day fall and the Hold initiations reflect doubt about growth. The specific line (voice growth reaccelerating or not) is not in any consensus aggregator, which carries only total revenue and EPS. Sized small because a crowded short (16% of shares, 7 DTC) dampens a negative.
evidence.independence: This shares the Q2 transcript with finding 1 but reads a different line (Voice Solutions reported growth vs cloud-communications guide conservatism). The two can both be true: the guide can be raised while voice stays slow. Nothing independent points the same way.

evidence.text: The 2026 midterm cycle is generating record-looking political texting: 'tens of billions' of political texts (Fox 13, 2026-10-05) and phones 'blowing up' in Alaska (Alaska Public, 2026-10-15). Political upside beyond that assumption would show in Q3 programmable messaging and in the Q4 guide (the election is 2026-11-03). Net of the rest: $13m is about 1.4% of the $905m FY revenue, so even a 50% political beat is under 1% of revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The political cut from $15m to $13m was one of the cited reasons for the -29.3% Q2 2026 reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company guided political down three months ago and no aggregator tracks Bandwidth's share of campaign SMS. evidence.text: Q3 2026 earnings build from primary documents gives about $1.40-1.80 EPS against a $0.91-1.07 consensus. Two inputs drive it. First, Q3 had no US hurricane landfall: Isaias on 2026-10-09 was the first US hurricane since 2024, so it falls in Q4. Second, the 1 June 2026 CAT XOL program costs $367.5m against $430.7m, saving $63.2m a treaty year, or about $15.8m pre-tax a quarter (about $0.40 a share after tax on about 30m diluted shares), and Q3 is the first full quarter of it. The comparable is Q3 2025: $1.63 EPS with zero catastrophe losses, $13.8m net weather, $5.0m favorable prior-year development (PYD) and a 46.1% ceded ratio. Q2 2026 already showed a 42.7% ceded ratio with only one month of the new program. Even with zero PYD and a loss ratio 5-7 points worse than Q3 2025, the build stays above $1.30.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have mostly been bought: Q2 2026 $2.05 vs $0.99 rose +16.47%, Q3 2025 (zero cat, $1.63) rose +12.48%, Q4 2025 rose +17.90% (baseline). The exception is Q1 2026: EPS +20% y/y to $1.19, but the stock fell -20.05%, alongside policies -6.3% and GPW -2.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.91-1.07 is below Q3 2025's $1.63 in a quarter with a lighter reinsurance bill and no landfall. If the street had marked the reinsurance saving and the benign quarter, the FY estimate would be well above $5.38 and the quarter near $1.5. The counter: the stock beat by 107% last quarter, so buy-side expectations are likely above the printed consensus. That is why this is sized well under the 14.5% median reaction.
evidence.independence: Supported by different documents. The CAT XOL release (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2026-05-28-Heritage-Announces-Full-Placement-of-2026-2027-CAT-XOL-Reinsurance-Program, 2026-05-28) gives the $367.5m cost and the $50m SE / $38m NE retention. The Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312525267080/d768057dex991.htm) is the comparable. The no-Q3-landfall fact is from https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/catastrophe/isaias-claims-begin-as-panhandle-counts-damage-from-first-us-hurricane-since-2024-593078.aspx (October 2026). Peer UVE's print is filed separately as F2.

evidence.text: Peer Universal Insurance (UVE) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-22, after Heritage last spoke. GAAP EPS was $1.80 vs $1.38 and adjusted $1.93 vs $1.36. The ceded premium ratio fell 5.1 points to 27.6%, attributed explicitly to the 1 June 2026 reinsurance program, and the net loss ratio fell 5.6 points. That confirms the cheaper-reinsurance mechanism flowing through a Florida homeowners P&L in Q3. Two cautions: UVE's Florida direct premiums written fell 3.3%, and its stock moved only $48.40 to $48.84 (+0.9%) the next session and drifted down about 4% after.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the peer's reaction on the same line: a ~23% EPS surprise driven by cheaper reinsurance bought +0.9% next day (Yahoo UVE daily closes 10-22 48.40, 10-23 48.84, 10-28 ~46.92). HRTG's own reactions to beats are larger (see F1).
evidence.why_not_priced: HRTG rose from $36.98 to $37.70 around UVE's print, then fell back below $36, so the read-through has not been bid into HRTG. The peer's muted reaction is the strongest sign that a reinsurance-driven beat is partly expected across the group. That is why this is a small positive and not a second copy of F1.
evidence.independence: Different company and different document from F1. It corroborates the mechanism but shares the same driver (the 2026 reinsurance market softening), so it is sized small to avoid counting one fact twice.

evidence.text: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida on 2026-10-09 as a Category 2 (Q4, after the quarter). Florida OIR counted 46,509 claims and $582m of insured losses as of 2026-10-15. Modelers put US private insured losses at $1-4.5bn (Cotality $2-3bn, KCC about $3bn). UVE said claims were 'less significant than initially anticipated'. Heritage's retention under the 2026-27 program is about $50m in the Southeast, before any Osprey Re reduction, which caps Heritage's net hit. Heritage will likely give a Q4 estimate in the release or on the 10-29 call. Against an implied Q4 consensus of about $1.10 ($5.38 FY less $3.23 H1 less about $1.05 Q3), a net retained loss of $15-40m pre-tax ($0.40-1.00 a share) could pull Q4 estimates down.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HRTG print in this baseline window carried a post-quarter landfall estimate. The tape is the evidence: HRTG rose +8% from landfall day to 10-22, so the market read Isaias as small or inside retention.
evidence.why_not_priced: Heritage has not quantified its Panhandle exposure or an Isaias loss, and the OIR exposure tables (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2026/10/08/888368.htm, 2026-10-08) do not list it. If the market had priced a large retained loss, HRTG would not have rallied 8% after landfall. The risk is a number at the top of retention, which would be news. This is macro-to-company transmission with no Heritage confirmation, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Retention figure from the company's 2026-05-28 CAT XOL release (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2026-05-28-Heritage-Announces-Full-Placement-of-2026-2027-CAT-XOL-Reinsurance-Program). UVE's 'less significant than anticipated' comment is from its 10-22 8-K (F2's document). Loss estimates are from https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/catastrophe/cotality-puts-isaias-insured-losses-at-2-billion-to-3-billion-below-prelandfall-estimates-593232.aspx (2026-10-12).

evidence.text: Top line and policy count are still shrinking. Q2 2026: gross premiums written -5.5% to $388.4m, policies in force -5.2% to 350,887, premiums in force -1.4%, commercial residential -12.7% on 'competitive pricing pressure' in Florida. Management said it 'anticipates a return to policy count growth' and that commercial premiums would 'level off in the second half'. Peer UVE's Florida direct premiums written fell 3.3% in Q3, and an Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-20) is headlined 'Heritage Faces A Tougher Quarter As Reserve-Release Tailwind Fades And Growth Gets Tested'. Q2's $23.4m favorable PYD (about $0.60 a share) is unlikely to repeat at that size. The Q3 test is whether the promised policy-count turn shows up.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 is the case: EPS +20% y/y, but policies -6.3% and GPW -2.6% on Florida competition, and the stock fell -20.05%. Q2 2026 GPW was -5.5%, but EPS doubled consensus and the stock rose +16.47%. So a shrinking top line is sold when the EPS beat is not big enough to drown it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FY consensus of $5.38 is 14% below 2025's $6.25, so the street models fading reserve releases. It is not priced as an outcome: whether Q3 shows the promised policy-count turn is unknown, and the stock sits only 7.5% below its 52-week high, so a growth disappointment has room to bite. What would differ if fully priced: the stock would trade near Q1's post-print lows, not near the high.
evidence.independence: UVE's 10-22 8-K shows Florida direct premiums written -3.3% (different company: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/891166/000089116626000092/a3q26uveex-991xearningspre.htm). evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-08-11) management said Q3 would be used to assess the commercial initiatives (the July telehealth channel and the national Sarah Jessica Parker TV campaign) and refine investment allocation, and that capital allocation will stay disciplined. Adjusted SG&A had already fallen 14% from Q1 to $34.9M. So the Q3 release is the first point at which a spend reset or reallocation could be announced. With 31.42M shares at $3.14, market cap is about $99M against $220M of cash at June 30 (about $175-185M estimated at Sep 30 after roughly $38-45M quarterly burn): the stock prices continued burn, and a credible cut that extends runway is worth more than the same news at a normal valuation.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior spend-guidance event. The name has fallen on 4 of its last 5 prints (-23.5% Q3'25, -6.6% Jan, -17.9% Q4'25, -20.8% Q1'26, -3.3% Q2'26), each time on launch numbers rather than on cost.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company has given no opex guidance at all (Q2 release), so the street has no number to update. A price at about 0.55x estimated cash with EV around -$80M says the market expects the burn to continue. If it expected a cut, the stock would not have fallen 47% since Sep 4 with no news.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000051/a991q226pressrelease.htm) confirms SG&A of $39.4M including $4.4M of SBC and $220.0M cash. The share count comes from the Q2 10-Q cover (31,420,343 at 2026-08-05). The 'assess and refine' wording is from Quartr's AI summary of the call, not a transcript. The sign is genuinely two-way: the reassessment could also produce a launch reset that is read as failure.

evidence.text: The liquidity language weakened between the 10-Qs. The Q1 2026 10-Q said cash was 'anticipated to fund the Company to positive operating cash flow'. The Q2 10-Q says only that cash 'will allow us to continue to commercialize VIZZ' and 'at least the next 12 months', and warns that capital could be used sooner than expected. The $150M ATM was fully used by Dec 2025 and there is no new ATM. Operating cash burn was $33.6M in Q1 and $38.7M in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The change was public on 2026-08-11, and the stock moved -3.3% over that print window. Its effect since is not separable from the general bleed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. It is a footnote and MD&A change no aggregator carries, but it has been public for 11 weeks. It matters again if the Q3 10-Q or release adds a financing step (a new ATM or shelf) or cuts the runway language further. On the financing question: the money funds the TV and DTC launch, not visible demand, since product revenue is $1.7M a quarter against about $40M of spend.
evidence.independence: Q1 10-Q wording: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000037/lenz-20260331.htm. Both readings are from company filings. This finding pulls against finding 1, because a cost cut is the remedy the dropped wording points to, so it is sized small and net of that.

evidence.text: July prescriptions reportedly grew more than 45% month on month after the telehealth channel and the national TV campaign launched (Q2 call, per Quartr's AI summary). Q2 product revenue was $1.736M on about 27,000 packs, +9% on Q1. Over 13,000 prescribers, about 75% of whom wrote more than once, and over 60% of e-pharmacy patients refill. So Q3 product revenue should step up from $1.74M, plausibly to $2.3-3.0M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product revenue has been the line this stock trades on: the Q4'25 revenue miss ($1.59M vs $3.09M est) brought -17.9%, and Q1'26 (an EPS miss) -20.8%. Q2's headline beat was licence-driven and the stock still fell 3.3%. This name sells prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Weekly script data (IQVIA/Symphony) is visible to the buy-side, and the 47% slide since Sep 4 plus Piper's PT cut suggest the August-September trend did not hold July's step. So this is mostly priced, and it is filed small. The visible tell would have been a rally after Aug 12; instead the stock went from $5.04 to $3.14.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release (SEC 8-K) confirms packs, prescribers and refill figures but describes growth only as 'accelerating'. The +45% figure is single-source (an AI summary).

evidence.text: Q3 revenue consensus is $4.20M (MarketBeat), against Q2 product sales of $1.736M. Reaching it needs either 2.4x product growth or about $1.5M+ of licence revenue. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4'25 revenue miss brought -17.9%. In Q2'26 a licence-driven revenue 'beat' ($5.49M vs $2.38M) still brought -3.3%, so the market looks through licence revenue in both directions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bar is single-source and probably stale (it may carry licence assumptions). Anyone modelling product revenue already expects a miss on it, which is why the size is capped. If the market were anchored on $4.20M of product revenue, the stock would not sit at 0.55x cash.
